fatal_errors: The proposed experimental DSC–ultrasonic–PVT workflow does not reconstruct the target DFT/MTP/FEP free-energy method or its replacement of EAM-based thermodynamic integration.
No supporting prior evidence is cited for the claimed 2–3% uncertainty, improvement over standalone DSC, or broad applicability across high-entropy alloys.

Ultrasonic elastic measurements do not by themselves determine liquid density, volume change on melting, or a complete set of liquid thermodynamic properties; the required thermodynamic inversion and independent calibration are unspecified.
The proposal does not address the extreme melting temperatures, chemical reactivity, evaporation, crucible contamination, or liquid containment challenges relevant to refractory TaVCrW.
It omits the decisive target benchmark: FEP-versus-TI free-energy agreement within 0.5 meV/atom and the quantified electronic and short-range-order contributions.
explanation: The response is aligned only at the broad level of seeking melting and liquid thermodynamic properties. It instead proposes an unsupported experimental alternative, whereas the target concerns an MTP-assisted DFT free-energy framework using FEP to replace costly EAM/TI calculations for disordered BCC TaVCrW. None of the target conditions, including 0 GPa, 2000–2400 K SRO calculations, 3456-atom cells, GGA-PBE/LDA, or sub-meV/atom MTP accuracy, are recovered. The expected 80% computational saving, approximately 20-fold acceleration, electronic-excitation shifts of 48–57 K, and 2.4 meV/atom SRO stabilization are also absent. The proposed falsification rule is quantitative enough to be testable, but it relies on vague literature benchmarks and does not establish independent reference methods for all inferred quantities. The single-phase limitation is reasonable but incomplete, and the absence of cited evidence makes the accuracy claims scientifically unsupported.
